title: feat: redesign quarto.org and the gallery
description:
This pull request redesigns quarto.org, with the new gallery as one part of it.

The theme takes every colour from one palette, `quartoorg-palette.scss`, through `--qorg-*` custom properties, and dark mode is navy everywhere.
The whole site now uses one brand colour, Posit blue, so the navbar, breadcrumbs, headings, cards and the current page in the sidebar and table of contents all look the same in every section.
Sidebar rows share the table of contents row style: the same size, spacing and highlight.
A code block with a filename now has a strip that matches the block, one shade darker and with the same rounding.

The gallery replaces the carousel with a landing and six category pages, built from YAML under `docs/gallery/data/`.
The landing has the gallery sidebar like any other page, one heading style, and cards with a thin top bar in the category colour, taken from the Posit palette.
Cards keep only the clickable category pills.
On the home page, "Where do you want to go?" now follows "Hello, Quarto".

Accessibility drove the details.
Body text and links reach 7:1, every control shows the same 2px focus ring, bars and the current row stay visible in forced colours mode, and a full-site axe scan finds nothing new.

title: Add webmcp extension to the listing
description:
Adds [webmcp](https://github.com/alexanderwiebe/quarto-webmcp) to `shortcodes-and-filters.yml`, between `watermark` and `webr`.

It is a filter extension for HTML output that exposes a site's content to in-browser AI agents through [WebMCP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp). Every page registers tools for the site's pages, posts and search. A post with an `agent:` block in its front matter also gets tools for its summary, audience, claims and evidence, and sources. A post-render script writes a search index and an `llms.txt`.

Listing requirements: hosted on GitHub, README with install steps and usage examples, MIT license (`LICENSE`), and an `example.qmd`. Latest release: v0.2.0. CI renders the example site and `example.qmd` with the current Quarto release and pre-release. In use on https://systemsbyaj.com.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Make release-merge skill the tool for release checklist step 9
description:
At release time, the merge of `prerelease` into `main` (step 9 of quarto-cli's `dev-docs/checklist-make-a-new-quarto-release.md`) was described in two places: quarto-cli's `make-release` skill and this repo's `release-merge` skill. The two drifted apart, and `make-release` never pointed to `release-merge`, so during the 1.11 release it was found only by chance when the merge hit conflicts.

`release-merge` now carries the commands for that step, taken from `make-release`: a drift check against `main`, the `docs/cli/cli-info.json` version check, the merge with a conflict table, and a `git diff --stat upstream/prerelease HEAD` check before pushing. A companion quarto-cli PR makes `make-release` hand the step to this skill instead of repeating the commands.

Where the skill differed from the checklist, it now follows it:

- `cli-info.json` is checked on `prerelease` before the merge, and regenerated there only when its version is not the stable version. Regenerating it after the merge put a commit on `main` that `prerelease` never gets.
- Conflicts resolve to `prerelease`, except `_axe-report.md` which keeps `main`. The previous "keep `main` where it is a strict superset" rule is replaced by the drift check, which brings such commits to `prerelease` before merging.
- The Axe Report runs after `main` is merged back into `prerelease`. It commits to both branches, so running it earlier breaks the fast-forward.

Updates `korthout/backport-action` from 4.6.0 to 4.7.0
Release notes

Sourced from korthout/backport-action's releases.

Backport-action v4.7.0

What's Changed

Thanks to a great contribution by @​lexfrei, backports no longer fail when the target branch already contains some of the changes, for example if a specific commit was already manually cherry-picked, or on a re-run. Previously, git reported the empty cherry-pick as a conflict, so the backport failed (or opened a draft PR with conflict_resolution: draft_commit_conflicts).

Now the action skips those commits:

  • Some commits already on the target: the backport PR is created as usual. The comment on the original pull request mentions the skipped commits, and a comment on the backport PR lists them.
  • All commits already on the target: there's nothing to backport, so no PR is created. The target is skipped, just like when its backport PR already exists, and doesn't count as a failure in was_successful.

With comment_style: summary, that looks like this:

Target Status
stable/8.7 :white_check_mark: Created #612 — 1 commit skipped (target already contains changes)
stable/8.6 :heavy_minus_sign: Skipped (target already contains changes)

No configuration needed to enable this. This is a bug fix released in a new minor version to avoid surprising users with new behavior.

  • Skip commits the target branch already contains by @​lexfrei in korthout/backport-action#705

New Contributors

Updates `korthout/backport-action` from 4.6.0 to 4.7.0
Release notes

Sourced from korthout/backport-action's releases.

Backport-action v4.7.0

What's Changed

Thanks to a great contribution by @​lexfrei, backports no longer fail when the target branch already contains some of the changes, for example if a specific commit was already manually cherry-picked, or on a re-run. Previously, git reported the empty cherry-pick as a conflict, so the backport failed (or opened a draft PR with conflict_resolution: draft_commit_conflicts).

Now the action skips those commits:

  • Some commits already on the target: the backport PR is created as usual. The comment on the original pull request mentions the skipped commits, and a comment on the backport PR lists them.
  • All commits already on the target: there's nothing to backport, so no PR is created. The target is skipped, just like when its backport PR already exists, and doesn't count as a failure in was_successful.

With comment_style: summary, that looks like this:

Target Status
stable/8.7 :white_check_mark: Created #612 — 1 commit skipped (target already contains changes)
stable/8.6 :heavy_minus_sign: Skipped (target already contains changes)

No configuration needed to enable this. This is a bug fix released in a new minor version to avoid surprising users with new behavior.

title: [Sync to prerelease] docs: recommend a-4f with ua-2 for tagged LaTeX PDF output
description:
# Description
Sync of #2325 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### docs: recommend a-4f with ua-2 for tagged LaTeX PDF output
Follow-up to #2317, which used `a-3a` in its example because `a-2a` fails veraPDF with tagged LaTeX output. The supported standards table still lists `a-2a`, and nothing tells users which PDF/A level to pick when they want a tagged PDF.

LaTeX tagging targets PDF 2.0, and by default it embeds two CSS files (`latex-list-css.html`, `latex-align-css.html`) as associated files. With LuaLaTeX, display equations also embed MathML files. PDF/A-2 and plain PDF/A-4 only allow embedded files that are themselves PDF/A, so `a-2a` fails veraPDF clause 6.8-5 and `a-4` fails clause 6.9. `a-4f` allows these files and is the PDF/A level based on PDF 2.0, as suggested in latex3/tagging-project#1676.

The LaTeX part of the shared `_pdf-standard.md` partial now has a "PDF/A and LaTeX Tagging" section that recommends `pdf-standard: [a-4f, ua-2]` and explains the failure. It also documents `\tagpdfsetup{attach-css=false}` for users who need `a-2a` or `a-4`, with its limit: it removes the CSS files but not the MathML ones, so a document with display math still fails. The tagging bullet no longer uses `a-2a` as its example. The Typst page is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- [x] With Quarto 1.11.8 and its bundled veraPDF 1.28.2, `[a-4f, ua-2]` with `documentclass: article` passes `4f` and `ua2`
- [x] `a-2a` fails `6.8-5`; with `attach-css=false` it passes `2a` without display math and still fails `6.8-5` with display math (`mathml-1.xml` embedded)
- [x] Render `pdf-basics.qmd` and `typst.qmd`: new section and anchor only on the LaTeX page; both pages use the Markdown engine, no freeze changes

Related to latex3/tagging-project#1676

title: docs(typst): document code annotations and the filename bar
description:
Documents code annotations and the `filename` attribute for Typst output, added in:
- quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14170

The code annotation page gets a Typst tab with a screenshot and a prerelease callout for 1.12.
It also says that `hover` and `select` use the same layout as `below` in Typst, and that the Typst format supports annotations.
The HTML code page now says that Typst shows the filename in a bar above the code block, and its `_freeze` entry is refreshed for that sentence.
The markdown basics page says the same next to the `filename` example.

The Typst custom format page gets a "Code Blocks" section for format and filter authors.
It describes `quarto-code-filename`, which draws a code block with a filename, and the `quarto-code-block-style` state, which holds the inset, radius and outline of code blocks.
Its example draws a frame around a code block with a filename, and I rendered that example with a Quarto build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14170.

The pull request targets `prerelease`, because the feature is new in 1.12.
I rendered the changed pages on their own with `quarto render`, not the whole site, and the new text, callouts and screenshot appear in the output.

The screenshot is from a Typst render of the existing penguins example.

title: Document section titles and equation names as link text
description:
Documents quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15249 (closes quarto-dev/quarto-cli#1196 and quarto-dev/quarto-cli#4532 there), new in 1.11.

Adds a "Titles as Link Text" subsection at the end of the References section of `docs/authoring/cross-references.qmd`, marked with `{{< prerelease-callout 1.11 >}}`:

- An empty link to a section, `[](#sec-introduction)`, shows the section's title.
- An equation's new `name` attribute, `{#eq-energy name="..."}`, is shown by `[](#eq-energy)`; an equation without a name falls back to "Equation 1".
- It works in all formats and across chapters of a book; links with their own text and `@sec-…` references are unchanged.

The example is shown as source with a Syntax/Output table, not rendered live, so the page renders the same before and after the quarto-cli PR is merged.

The page uses the Jupyter engine, so `_freeze/docs/authoring/cross-references/execute-results/html.json` is updated too. The plot image in the freeze is unchanged (my local re-render produced a byte-different but equivalent PNG, which I left out).

This PR and #2327 (labels on rows of multi-row equations) edit different sections of the same page, so the `.qmd` changes merge cleanly, but both regenerate the page's freeze file, which will conflict. Whichever PR merges second needs its freeze regenerated with both sections; I'll do that once the first one is merged.

Rendered and checked locally with a dev build of the quarto-cli branch.

- **AI tool used**: Claude Code
- **Codebase grounding**: local clones of quarto-cli and quarto-web, quarto-web's README and `_style-guide.md`
- **Human review**: I have reviewed, tested, and verified the AI-generated content before submitting.

title: fix(review-extension-prs): validate revealjs-plugins and more contributes paths
description:
`validate-extension.sh` checks the files an extension's `contributes` block points at, but it skipped several shapes. An inline revealjs plugin whose `script` or `stylesheet` pointed at a missing file printed "no file references found" and passed. The generic walk also descended into the plugin's config, so keys like `css` or `template` inside it were reported as missing files. `template-partials`, `include-*` entries written as `{file: path}`, and `.scss` entries under `theme` were not checked either, so a missing `custom.scss` only failed at render time.

Reference resolution was also looser than quarto-cli's. quarto-cli joins every reference onto the extension directory, and `quarto add` installs only that directory. The script however:

1. Accepted a file at the repository root, so `script.js` passed when only a root-level copy existed.
2. Accepted `../root.js` when that file existed in the repo, although it is missing after install.
3. Stripped every leading dot and slash from a path, so `.custom.scss` was checked as `custom.scss`.
4. Recorded `../foo/filter.lua` as `foo/../foo/filter.lua` in the reverse Lua check, so a used filter was reported as dead code.

All references now resolve through one `ext_path()` helper that normalises with `posixpath.normpath` and resolves against the extension directory only. A reference that climbs out of the extension directory fails with its own message, because "missing from repo" would be wrong for a file the repo does contain. A reference that climbs out and back in (`../foo/x.js`) still resolves inside the extension and passes.

The `revealjs-plugins` handling follows `src/extension/extension.ts` in quarto-cli: inline `script`/`stylesheet` paths resolve against the extension directory, a string or `{plugin: dir}` entry must name a directory holding `plugin.yml`, and a string under `formats` first resolves to an embedded extension. `{plugin: .}` is allowed and names the extension directory itself.

The "no file references" INFO line now says the shape was not recognised, so it reads as a gap in the check and not a clean result. `SKILL.md` step 8 lists the keys the script actually checks.

## Test Plan

- [x] `self-test.sh` offline fixtures cover each plugin shape, the other new contributes shapes, root-level files, parent-relative paths, dot-prefixed names and `{plugin: .}` (67 passed, 0 failed)
- [x] Network cases against `quarto-ext/pointer` and `quarto-ext/attribution` cover scalar and list `script`/`stylesheet`

title: [Sync to prerelease] docs: explain KOMA default class vs standard classes for pdf-standard
description:
# Description
Sync of #2317 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### docs: explain KOMA default class vs standard classes for pdf-standard
With `pdf-standard` set, Quarto's default KOMA-Script classes produce a PDF that declares the standard and passes veraPDF, but the structure tagging is incomplete: headings are tagged as plain paragraphs (`P`) instead of `H2`/`H3`. Since the KOMA-Script 3.49.3 abort was overridden in quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15154 (backport quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15158), this is the behavior that ships in 1.10.20 and 1.11, and nothing in the docs tells users a standard class is needed for an accessible PDF.

The PDF accessibility section now explains this and recommends `documentclass: article` (or `report`/`book` for books) for `ua-2` or a PDF/A "a" level. It lives in the LaTeX-only part of the shared `_pdf-standard.md` partial, so the Typst page is unchanged. PDF Basics also documents the KOMA options Quarto sets by default (`DIV=11`, captions above tables) and that they are silently ignored with a standard class, and the books page points to the new section.

Checked by rendering with Quarto 1.11.8 and KOMA-Script 3.49.3: `scrartcl` and `scrreprt` produce `P` tags for headings, `article` and `report` produce `H2`/`H3` inside `Sect`, and all four pass veraPDF `ua2`. With `article`, `classoption: DIV=9` only gives `Unused global option(s): [DIV]` in the LaTeX log.

The LaTeX tagging project lists `scrartcl` and `scrbook` as currently incompatible with tagging (latex3/tagging-project#1118, [tagging status](https://latex3.github.io/tagging-project/tagging-status/#classes)).

The example uses `a-3a` rather than `a-2a`, because `a-2a` currently fails veraPDF clause 6.8 with every document class: LaTeX tagging attaches two CSS files, and PDF/A-2 only allows embedded files that are themselves PDF/A. That's a separate issue from the class choice, reported upstream in latex3/tagging-project#1676.

Related to quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14422

title: docs: add Deno 2.9.8 security update to 1.11 highlights
description:
Quarto 1.11 updates its bundled Deno from 2.7.14 to 2.9.8 for a security reason: Deno 2.7.14 still trusted the compromised eMudhra / emSign intermediate certificate authorities, so an attacker on the network could impersonate any HTTPS site to `quarto publish`, `quarto add`, `quarto use template`, `quarto install`, and TypeScript scripts run by Quarto.

The 1.11 highlights get a "Dependency updates:" entry, in the same format as the 1.8 highlights, linking the Mozilla bug, the incident site, and the Deno fix (denoland/deno#37046). The entry replaces the placeholder text left from the previous release cycle.

Targets `prerelease` because the change only applies to the upcoming version.

title: docs: document installed extension layout and qualified names
description:
Follow-up to quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15111. Extensions are installed under `_extensions/<owner>/<name>/`, where the owner is the GitHub owner the extension is installed from. Archives and local directories have no owner and install as `_extensions/<name>/`.

This was only written in the unpublished draft `docs/journals/_draft/create-extensions.qmd`, which also shows an owner folder in the source layout. Quarto drops that folder at install time. Several extension repositories ship `_extensions/<owner>/<name>/` anyway, and a `template.qmd` using a qualified format name then fails when the template is used from a local copy.

`docs/extensions/distributing.qmd` now covers:

- source layout without an owner folder, with a 1.11 callout for the install note added in quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15117
- installed layout per install source. GitHub archive URLs keep their owner, so the previous "they all share a single namespace" sentence was not accurate for them
- how `<owner>/<name>` and bare names match, and using the bare name in a `template.qmd` shipped with an extension
- `quarto add --embed` for bundling an extension from another owner, which was only in the CLI reference until now

Also `quarto install` is replaced by `quarto add` in `starter-templates.qmd`, and `managing.qmd` now shows the installed paths.

Each statement was checked against quarto-cli source (`src/extension/install.ts`, `extension-host.ts`, `extension.ts`) and with real installs in 1.11: GitHub repository, GitHub archive URL, local directory, and `--embed`.

Related to quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15111

title: docs: cover page range splitting for citation references

title: [Sync to prerelease] Add readable-resume to custom formats
description:
# Description
Sync of #2299 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Add readable-resume to custom formats
Adds [readable-resume](https://github.com/supertj/quarto-readable-resume), a one-page resume format built on Typst.

The design is the Classic template from ReadableResume, a resume template site I run, where it's offered for Google Docs and Word. Serif type, centered section headings over a thin rule, one column with no tables or icons, so the text comes out of the PDF in reading order, which is what applicant tracking systems parse. It's a plainer style than awesomecv-typst, closer to what university career offices hand out.

The extension is two Typst partials plus a short Lua filter that turns entry divs like `::: {.experience company="..."}` into Typst function calls. No network or file access. It's MIT licensed, and the README has `quarto use template` and `quarto add` commands and a usage example. Tested with Quarto 1.10.19 and 1.7.34 (1.7 is the minimum because the template needs Typst 0.12 or later).

The author link goes to readableresume.com rather than my GitHub profile, since that's where the design comes from. If you'd rather keep author links pointing to GitHub, I'll change it to https://github.com/supertj.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Fix older publishes overwriting newer deploys
description:
# Description
Sync of #2294 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Fix older publishes overwriting newer deploys
Deploys of the same site from different workflows do not wait for each other. `publish.yml` grouped its concurrency by calling workflow and ref, so a publish from a push to `main`, from `update-downloads.yml` and from the axe report each ran in their own group, and an older build finishing last could overwrite a newer deploy.

This becomes more frequent with #2293, where sync PRs are merged right away and publish `prerelease` themselves.

## Fix

There is now one concurrency group per deployed site, quarto.org and prerelease.quarto.org, whichever workflow calls `publish.yml`. The site is picked the same way the deploy steps pick it, so a caller passing `prerelease: false` from the `prerelease` branch (the axe report dispatched there) still lands in the quarto.org group. A dispatch of `publish.yml` from any other branch deploys neither site, so it gets its own group and never cancels a deploy.

In a shared group, the run that queues last cancels the one in progress. Every publish now checks out the branch tip when the job starts instead of a fixed commit, so the run that wins includes every earlier change. `update-downloads.yml` and `axe-scan.yml` pass the branch name instead of the commit they just pushed, and push-triggered runs check out `github.ref` instead of `github.sha`.

The render profile had the same problem, already on `main`. A called workflow inherits the caller's ref, so the axe report dispatched from `prerelease` rendered its quarto.org publish with the `prerelease-docs` profile, and quarto.org was deployed with prerelease branding and site URLs. The profile is now picked with the same guard as the prerelease deploy step, so `prerelease: false` always renders the release profile.

## Test Plan

- [x] `zizmor` and `actionlint` on the workflows: no new findings
- [ ] After merge, the next push to `main` publishes quarto.org from the branch tip
- [ ] After merge, the next `Update Downloads` run with changes publishes both sites

title: [Sync to prerelease] Merge sync PRs to prerelease right away and retry failed backports
description:
# Description
Sync of #2293 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Merge sync PRs to prerelease right away and retry failed backports
Since the v1.10 release merge, the automatic backport to `prerelease` failed for every PR merged to `main` (#2141, #2227, #2235, #2257, #2258, #2222). The changes reached `prerelease` only through manual backports later (#2271, #2290), #2141 about two months after it merged.

## Root Cause

Most failures were not real divergence between the branches but an ordering race. A sync PR stays open on `prerelease` until someone merges it, from minutes to many hours. When a second PR to `main` touches the same file in the meantime, it is cherry-picked onto a `prerelease` that does not have the first change yet, and conflicts.

- #2141 conflicted on `_freeze/docs/authoring/tables/` because the sync PR of #2138 (#2142) merged 19 seconds after it.
- #2235 conflicted on `styles.css` because the sync PRs of #2233 and #2234 merged 20 minutes later.

A failed backport is never retried, so it then breaks every later PR on the same files: #2227 failed on #2141, #2258 and #2257 on #2235. Only #2222 was a real conflict, as #2272 had already changed the same page on `prerelease`.

## Fix

When the cherry-pick applies cleanly, the workflow now merges the sync PR immediately and publishes `prerelease` by calling `publish.yml`, as a merge made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not fire the push event. It publishes the branch tip, not the merge commit, so two syncs landing close together still deploy the latest content.

When the cherry-pick fails, the source PR gets the new `backport-failed` label, so `gh pr list --label backport-failed --state merged` lists what is missing from `prerelease`. A sync PR that fails to merge, because `prerelease` moved between the cherry-pick and the merge, gets the label too and is left open for a manual merge.

After each sync merge, and after any PR merged by hand into `prerelease`, the workflow comments `/sync-prerelease` on the oldest `backport-failed` PR. A backport that only waited on an earlier change then applies on its own, and the chain moves to the next one. It stops at the first PR that fails again, which needs a manual backport and the label removed afterwards.

No concurrency group is used: GitHub cancels a pending run when another one queues, which would drop a backport silently when several PRs merge within a few minutes.

As sync PRs are no longer reviewed before merging, a PR that must not reach `prerelease` (like #1983 for v1.9 only) now needs the `no-sync-prerelease` label before it is merged into `main`. Leaving the sync PR unmerged is no longer possible.

Direct pushes to `main` are still not synced. That is left for another PR.

## Test Plan

- [x] `zizmor` and `actionlint` on the workflow: no new findings in the CI audit
- [x] Run the `gh` queries used by the workflow against this repo, read-only (label lookup, oldest labeled PR, empty result)
- [x] Create the `backport-failed` label
- [ ] After merge, the next PR to `main` gets its sync PR merged and `prerelease` published
- [ ] After merge, a failed backport gets the label, and a later sync triggers its retry

title: refactor: move the site theme and chrome into a local extension
description: This moves the site's theme, scripts, Lua filters and chrome into a local extension, `_extensions/quartoorg/`, used through a `quartoorg` project type. Pages no longer set a format; they inherit `quartoorg-html` from the project. Brand images move to `assets/images/`, and the old `/quarto.png` URL redirects, since the brand docs used it in an example. The page chooser shortcode and the accessibility fixes from `main` are part of the extension too, with their CSS now in the theme's SCSS. The site should look the same as before once deployed. (Locally it does, except notebook preview, see issue below) The one intended change is in dark mode, where borders now use `$gray-400`. That's 3.70:1 against the page instead of 1.08:1, so they're actually visible, and the chooser and tool tiles no longer need their own `#6c757d` override. An axe scan of the whole site finds the same issues as on `main`. A new check, `_tools/check-site-format.ts`, stops a `format: html` from quietly dropping the site theme again. It runs in CI and in the pre-commit hook, and it'll only block pull requests from forks once the `check-site-format` job is a required check. --- This is to centralise/harmonise all themes together and tidy up a bit the repository. This will help integrate https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/pull/2140 with more chrome consistency, while also helping maintaining/updating it. --- ## Caveat Notebook preview pages lose everything in the site format except the theme, so the Posit badge, the code copy buttons and the site's grid widths are missing there (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14954).

title: [Sync to prerelease] Add live-questions to the revealjs extension listing
description:
# Description
Sync of #2288 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Add live-questions to the revealjs extension listing
Replaces #2283, which closed when I deleted my fork by mistake. The change is the same.

Adds [live-questions](https://github.com/seandavi/quarto-revealjs-live-questions) to `revealjs.yml`.

It's a Quarto revealjs extension (Lua filter + Reveal plugin) for live audience questions: multiple-choice polls and quizzes, short-answer word clouds, and Likert/rating scales, written in Quarto markdown on the slide. When the presenter reaches a question slide, it opens, a QR code points the audience to a phone voting page, and results update on the slide.

Against the listing requirements:

1. Hosted on GitHub.
2. README covers installation (`quarto add seandavi/quarto-revealjs-live-questions`), syntax and usage, with examples and screenshots.
3. MIT licensed (bundled third-party code, qrcode-generator, is MIT; its notice ships in `_extensions/live-questions/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`).

On network access: the extension connects only to the `server:` the author configures (a WebSocket to a server they host themselves on Cloudflare Workers or Docker). With no `server:` it renders statically, and in PDF/non-HTML output questions render as plain lists. There is no telemetry, no default or hosted server, and no CDN; the QR library is bundled. This is described under "Privacy and limits" in the README.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

From the next Quarto release, an image path is resolved against the file it is written in (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15039). Before, a relative `website: image` in `_quarto.yml` was resolved from each page, so it broke for pages in subdirectories.

The Preview Images section now says that relative images set in `_quarto.yml` (`website: image`, and `image` under `website: open-graph` or `website: twitter-card`) are relative to the project directory. The feed options table says the same for the listing `feed: image`, which already behaved this way but was not documented.

Companion to quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15039

title: docs: explain how open-graph image-width and image-height apply
description:
Companion to quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15040, which fixes quarto-dev/quarto-cli#12016 for Quarto 1.11, and quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15050, which adds JPEG measurement.

The `image` rows of both social metadata tables said that `image-width` and `image-height` improve "your Twitter Card". Twitter Card metadata never uses a declared size, only Open Graph does. The Twitter Card row now points to the Open Graph section.

A new "Image Size" section under Open Graph explains how a declared size applies. With `site-url` set, Quarto measures local PNG and JPEG images and uses that size over a declared one, so declared sizes matter for remote images and formats Quarto can't measure, such as WebP or GIF. Sizes in `website: open-graph` describe the site image: a page that supplies its own image gets only the sizes in its own `open-graph` metadata, even when it repeats the site image.

That last part changes behavior for sites without `site-url`, where page images used to inherit the site sizes. The section shows how to restore them through page or `_metadata.yml` `open-graph` metadata.

This targets `prerelease` directly, as the behavior is new in 1.11.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Reserve the red announcement banner for prerelease and fix its contrast
description:
# Description
Sync of #2276 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Reserve the red announcement banner for prerelease and fix its contrast
The announcement banner colours were mixed up:

| Site | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (before) | `#447099` | `#ff0039` |
| `prerelease` (before) | `#ff0039` (Cosmo `$danger`) | `#ff0039` |

White on `#ff0039` gives 3.95:1. [WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#contrast-minimum) needs 4.5:1. The prerelease axe scan flags it on all 334 light/dark pages ([run 37517108158](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/actions/runs/37517108158)). `main` shows no finding only because it has no announcement now.

This PR reserves red for `prerelease`, in both modes:

- `theme-dark.scss`: the `main` dark banner is `#447099`, the same as light mode (5.22:1).
- `theme-prerelease-docs.scss` → `theme-prerelease-banner.scss`. The new name tells you that the file only styles the banner. The colour is `#e60033` (4.76:1).
- `_quarto-prerelease-docs.yml`: adds the banner file to the dark theme too.

These files are identical on `main` and `prerelease`, so the automatic backport should apply cleanly.

Verification:

- I rendered `404.qmd` with each profile and checked the compiled CSS. `main` has `#447099` in light and dark. `prerelease` has `#e60033` in light and dark, and it overrides the `#447099` rule.
- I ran a full prerelease scan with the same change (in #2275, before the split). `color-contrast :: #ffffff on #ff0039` cleared (1002 instances), with no regressions.

Conflicts with #2222, which moves these rules into `_extensions/quartoorg/scss/`.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Run the weekly axe scan on prerelease too
description:
# Description
Sync of #2265 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Run the weekly axe scan on prerelease too
Follow-up to #2259. The weekly axe scan now also scans `prerelease` and publishes its report on prerelease.quarto.org. The `main` scan does not change.

- `axe-scan.yml` (new) contains the old scan and publish jobs as a reusable workflow. It has the inputs `branch`, `site`, and `prerelease`. For `prerelease`, it renders with the `prerelease-docs` profile, the same as `publish.yml`.
- `axe-report.yml` is now a two-leg matrix that calls `axe-scan.yml` once for `main` and once for `prerelease`. Each leg has its own concurrency group and artifact, so the two legs run in parallel.
- The `/release-merge` skill now has a note: a release merge conflicts on `_axe-report.md`. Keep the `main` version, then run the workflow manually.

Each leg commits `_axe-report.md` directly to its branch. These bot pushes do not make backport PRs.

Test run: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/actions/runs/37054502660

description:

- No regressions.

title: docs: document lof and lot for Typst output
description:
Document `lof: true` and `lot: true` for Typst output, which previously had no effect even though the options were advertised for the format. Quarto 1.11 makes them work for Typst documents (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15001, for quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14081).

The Typst page gets a "Lists of Figures and Tables" section with the pre-release callout, covering placement after the table of contents, title customization through the `lof-title` and `lot-title` crossref options or the document `lang`, and that subfigures are not listed separately. The cross-references page, which only described LaTeX raw commands, points to it. The custom formats page notes that a `typst-template.typ` reusing Quarto's `typst-show.typ` must accept the new parameters, otherwise Typst reports `unexpected argument: lof` when the option is set.

Typst books built on the bundled orange-book extension are not covered yet, since their lists still need an upstream fix; the docs for books can follow once that lands.

Targets `prerelease` because the feature ships in 1.11.

title: Backport five accessibility fixes to prerelease
description:
The automatic backport failed for these five PRs because of cherry-pick conflicts. This PR applies them to `prerelease` by hand, in the order that they merged:

- #2227 Fix skipped heading levels in markdown headings
- #2235 Fix contrast of the extensions chooser and listing description links
- #2258 Make the tool choosers consistent
- #2257 Close the listing-link rule so the visually-hidden code rule applies again
- #2141 Add iframe titles to embedded videos

I checked all PRs merged to `main` since 2026-07-01. These five are the only ones that are not on `prerelease`.

#2227 and #2141 had a conflict in `_freeze/docs/authoring/tables/execute-results/html.json`. After both PRs, the source of `tables.qmd` on `prerelease` is the same as on `main`. Thus this file is now the same as on `main`. The other freeze files from #2227 come from `main` without change, because their sources are the same on both branches.

## Axe scan

I rendered the site with `QUARTO_PROFILE=prerelease-docs` and scanned all 373 pages with `quarto call axe`. Then I compared the result with the prerelease scan of 2026-10-02 (run 37054502660).

- New (not baselined) findings: 32 → 4.
- All target signatures are gone: 19 `heading-order`, `color-contrast :: #5092dd on #ffffff`, and `link-in-text-block :: tr > td > .listing-description > a`.
- `frame-title :: iframe` decreased from 3 to 1 instance. The one that remains is on `code-annotation.html`, which #2141 does not change.
- The elephant `image-alt` and `link-name` findings on `markdown-basics.html` moved from `.odd` rows to `.even` rows. The prerelease baseline already has the `.even` signatures, so they are baselined.

These PRs do not fix the 4 findings that remain. The banner contrast (`#ffffff on #ff0039`, 334 pages) is separate work. The others are three `scrollable-region-focusable` signatures.

title: Scan the pages a PR changes with axe
description:
Adds an `axe` job to the preview workflow. It reuses the preview render and runs `quarto call axe` on the pages the PR changes. It fails on new serious or critical findings that are not in `_axe-baseline.json`.

- A change that can reach every page (SCSS, `_quarto.yml`, shared partials, extensions, the baseline) scans the whole site.
- Pages in `_axe-exclude.txt` are skipped.
- The site artifact uploads after the PR comment, so the preview links are not delayed.

Still to test: one PR that changes a single page, and one that changes SCSS (full-site scan).

title: docs: describe how metadata from different sources is merged
description:
Companion to quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14996, which makes a document's front matter merge with `_quarto.yml`, `_metadata.yml` and `metadata-files` instead of replacing their values for each top-level key it sets. The Metadata Merging section only said that objects and arrays are merged, so this documents the rules readers now depend on: arrays are combined with duplicates removed, a single value merged with a list is added to it, and which of an included file or its parent wins for a single value.

Pandoc's `--metadata-file` was not documented anywhere on the site. A short note in Metadata Includes says how it merges and links to the Pandoc manual.

Targets `prerelease` as the change ships in 1.11. Each documented behavior was checked by rendering small projects with a build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14996.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Baseline the Inputs.table empty header on the OJS data sources page
description:
# Description
Sync of #2268 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Baseline the Inputs.table empty header on the OJS data sources page
The weekly axe report shows one new finding: `empty-table-header` on `docs/interactive/ojs/data-sources.html`. It was also the only unmatched non-image finding in the 2026-10-02 run.

It is the known Observable Inputs problem. The `Inputs.table` select-all header cell holds only an unlabeled checkbox. The existing `empty-table-header :: th` entry already lists this page. But on this page axe anchors the selector to the table's id (`#oi-3a86ea-1 > table > thead > tr > th:nth-child(1)`), so the signature is `empty-table-header :: #oi-3a86ea > table > thead > tr > th` and does not match.

This PR adds an entry for that signature, scoped to the one page. The `3a86ea` namespace is fixed in Inputs, and the signature already drops the `-1` counter, so the signature is stable from run to run. When quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14934 updates Inputs, the namespace becomes `inputs-3a86ea`, and this entry must be replaced (same as the `Inputs.range` entries).

Runs: [2026-10-05](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/actions/runs/37270879423), [2026-10-02](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/actions/runs/37046059351).

This change will also need to go to `prerelease`.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Make the image examples in Markdown Basics match their output
description:
# Description
Sync of #2261 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Make the image examples in Markdown Basics match their output
The image rows in the Links & Images table of Markdown Basics showed code that did not match their output. In 2022, `fig-alt` was added to the output of three rows, but not to their code. The fourth row showed `fig-alt="Alt text"` in the code and a different description in the output.

Now the code and the output of each row are identical:

- Image, linked image, and linked image with a title: no `fig-alt`. Each row has an `<!-- a11y: no alt on purpose -->` comment.
- Linked image with no caption: `fig-alt="Elephant drawing."`

A new row, before the linked image, shows an image with a caption and `fig-alt="Elephant drawing."`. It makes no axe finding.

The images without alt text make axe findings. This PR adds six `intentional:` entries to `_axe-baseline.json`, limited to this page: two `image-alt` and two `link-name` for the linked image, and two `image-alt` for the plain image. The linked image with a title makes no finding, because axe uses the `title` as the name.

It also adds an "Intentional examples" section to `.claude/rules/axe-baseline.md`, and a sentence in `_style-guide.md` that points to it.

Scan of `docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html` (4 cells, all ok): before, 4 new findings and 1 known. After, 0 new and 7 known.

The baseline signatures include the `.odd` or `.even` class of the table row. If a row is added above these examples, update the signatures.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Add a weekly axe accessibility report for quarto.org
description:
# Description
Sync of #2259 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Add a weekly axe accessibility report for quarto.org
This PR adds a weekly accessibility scan of quarto.org and a page that shows the results.

## What it adds

- **`.github/workflows/axe-report.yml`.** Every Monday, and on demand, the workflow renders `main` and scans the site with `quarto call axe`. Then it commits the report to `_axe-report.md` and calls `publish.yml`. A push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not start `publish.yml`, so the workflow calls it directly, as `update-downloads.yml` does.
- **`accessibility/site-report.qmd`.** This page includes `_axe-report.md` under "Latest scan". The `shift-headings` filter moves the report's headings below the page headings.
- **`_axe-exclude.txt`.** This file lists the pages that the scan skips, with a reason for each. It is at the root of the repo, so local scans can use it too.
- **`filters/axe-page-links.lua`.** This filter links each page path in the report tables to the live page.
- **Git Link extension (`mcanouil/quarto-gitlink`).** The extension links `owner/repo#N` references in the report. The page sets `show-platform-badge: false`.

## How the workflow edits the report

Before the commit, the workflow:

- adds a line at the top with the scanned commit and the scan date. It uses `git rev-parse HEAD`, because the checkout is always `main`.
- removes the sentences that point to `README.md` and `findings.json`. These files are only in the workflow artifact.

If the scan does not complete, the workflow does not commit or publish the report. The `_axe-checks/` folder goes to a workflow artifact for 90 days, and it is in `.gitignore`.

## Notes for review

- `_axe-report.md` holds placeholder text until the first run.
- No link goes to the new page yet.
- The weekly commit changes `_axe-report.md` only on `main`. Expect small conflicts in this file at the release-time merge from `prerelease`.
- The link to the `quarto call axe` docs uses `prerelease-docs-url 1.11`, because these docs are only on prerelease.quarto.org for now.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Add an axe baseline for known third-party and upstream findings
description:
# Description Sync of #2208 to `prerelease`. ## Original PR ### Add an axe baseline for known third-party and upstream findings ## Summary This PR adds `_axe-baseline.json`, the baseline file for `quarto call axe` (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14815). A scan compares its findings with the baseline. It reports only the findings that are not in the baseline as new. The baseline has 128 signatures. Each one is a finding that quarto-web cannot fix in its own content, a false positive, or an intentional example: - `third-party:` the markup comes from a library, for example Observable Plot or leaflet. - `upstream:` the markup comes from Quarto, and a quarto-cli issue tracks the fix. - `false-positive:` axe reports a defect that a user does not see. - `intentional:` a docs example shows the defect on purpose. title: Close the listing-link rule so the visually-hidden code rule applies again
description:
#2235 left out the closing `}` of the `.listing-description a` rule in `styles.css`. Browsers support CSS nesting, so they read the #2234 rule as nested inside it, as `table.quarto-listing-table .listing-description a pre.sourceCode.visually-hidden`. That selector never matches. As a result, the screen-reader-only code blocks on the get-started Jupyter pages are scrollable regions again (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`, [WCAG 2.1.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#keyboard)).

This PR adds the `}`.

**Axe scan** (Quarto 1.11.4, the three get-started Jupyter pages plus `docs/extensions/listing-filters.html`, 1440×900 and 320×568, light and dark): 4 signatures (20 instances) cleared, 0 new. The listing-description links stay underlined.

title: Make the tool choosers consistent
description:
The five "Choose your tool" interfaces had different labels and markup, and copied CSS and JS. This PR makes them consistent.

- **Get started, manuscripts and extensions:** a new `page-chooser` shortcode (`_extensions/page-chooser/`) replaces three copies of the markup, CSS and script. Each chooser is now a `<nav>` named by a visible label, with `aria-current` on the active page. The items are in `_metadata.yml`.
- **`tools-tabset`:** `aria-labelledby` on the visible label replaces `aria-hidden` plus `aria-label`. A selected tab no longer changes size.
- **Landing cards:** `role="button"` is removed from the links. The manuscripts logos are decorative (`alt=""`). The cards now show a visible focus ring ([WCAG 2.4.7](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#focus-visible)).
- **CSS:** the inline `<style>` in the extensions chooser is removed. The `.tool` rules are the same in both `tutorial.css` files, and these rules no longer apply to other links on the page.
- "Editor" is now "Text Editor" in the get-started chooser, the same as on the landing page.

An axe scan of the same 32 pages before and after the change shows no new findings. Screenshots below.

# Description

# Description
Sync of #2236 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Fix the Citation Fields table markup on the citeable articles page
The Citation Fields table on the citeable articles page had broken markup.

- **`url` row:** One line was 3 characters too wide for its grid column. Pandoc then read the table as three columns. As a result, the `url` row was one cell that showed literal `|` characters, "Document Yaml" became an `<h1>`, and each row had an extra empty cell.
- **Lists in `<small>`:** `<small>` cannot contain a list. In the browser, the `container-title` list items lost their `<ul>` parent. axe reports `list` and `listitem` ([WCAG 1.3.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#info-and-relationships)).
- **Notes in `<sub>`:** 13 notes used `<sub>` as small print. Screen readers announce this text as subscript.

This PR has two commits:

1. Fix the markup. All notes are now `::: small` divs, the `url` row fits its column, and a `type:report` typo is fixed.
2. Convert the table to `list-table` syntax, so that column alignment cannot break it again.

The table now has a real header row and two columns. I did an axe scan of the page before and after. The `list` and `listitem` findings (3 instances) are gone, and nothing is new or worse.

**Check**

title: [Sync to prerelease] Stop screen-reader-only code blocks from being scrollable regions
description:
# Description
Sync of #2234 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Stop screen-reader-only code blocks from being scrollable regions

The get-started Jupyter pages have screen-reader-only code blocks (`{.markdown .visually-hidden}`, `{.yaml .visually-hidden}`). Each block is a 1px box that scrolls, so axe reports `scrollable-region-focusable` ([WCAG 2.1.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#keyboard)) on each one.

- **Cause:** Quarto's `pre.sourceCode { overflow-y: visible !important }` beats Bootstrap's `.visually-hidden { overflow: hidden !important }`. As a result, the box computes to `overflow-y: auto`.
- **Fix:** One rule in `styles.css` gives `overflow: hidden !important` back to `pre.sourceCode.visually-hidden`.
- **Why here:** quarto-cli#14816 will skip these blocks on purpose, and Quarto does not change Bootstrap utility classes that authors can use.

I did an axe scan before and after on the three pages. All 20 instances are gone, and nothing is new or worse. The hidden blocks stay 1×1 and clipped in light and dark mode, at 1440×900 and 320×568.

**Check**

- https://deploy-preview-2234.quarto.org/docs/get-started/hello/jupyter.html
- https://deploy-preview-2234.quarto.org/docs/get-started/computations/jupyter.html

title: Fix the Citation Fields table markup on the citeable articles page
description:
The Citation Fields table on the citeable articles page had broken markup.

- **`url` row:** One line was 3 characters too wide for its grid column. Pandoc then read the table as three columns. As a result, the `url` row was one cell that showed literal `|` characters, "Document Yaml" became an `<h1>`, and each row had an extra empty cell.
- **Lists in `<small>`:** `<small>` cannot contain a list. In the browser, the `container-title` list items lost their `<ul>` parent. axe reports `list` and `listitem` ([WCAG 1.3.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#info-and-relationships)).
- **Notes in `<sub>`:** 13 notes used `<sub>` as small print. Screen readers announce this text as subscript.

This PR has two commits:

1. Fix the markup. All notes are now `::: small` divs, the `url` row fits its column, and a `type:report` typo is fixed.
2. Convert the table to `list-table` syntax, so that column alignment cannot break it again.

The table now has a real header row and two columns. I did an axe scan of the page before and after. The `list` and `listitem` findings (3 instances) are gone, and nothing is new or worse.

**Check**

- https://deploy-preview-2236.quarto.org/docs/authoring/create-citeable-articles.html#citation-fields

title: Fix contrast of the extensions chooser and listing description links
description:

- **Category chooser tiles.** The tiles use a hard-coded `#5092dd`. On white, this is 3.23:1, and text needs 4.5:1 ([WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#contrast-minimum)). The tiles now use `var(--bs-link-color)`: 5.15:1 in light mode and 7.27:1 in dark mode.
- **Links in listing descriptions.** Quarto's listing-table styles remove link underlines. Only color marks these links, at 2.23:1 against the body text, and they need 3:1 ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#use-of-color)). A rule in `styles.css` underlines them again.

Checked with a full-site axe scan before and after: `color-contrast` on the tiles (20 instances) and `link-in-text-block` on the extensions pages (13 instances) are gone. Nothing is new or worse.

title: Stop screen-reader-only code blocks from being scrollable regions
description:
The get-started Jupyter pages have screen-reader-only code blocks (`{.markdown .visually-hidden}`, `{.yaml .visually-hidden}`). Each block is a 1px box that scrolls, so axe reports `scrollable-region-focusable` ([WCAG 2.1.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#keyboard)) on each one.

- **Cause:** Quarto's `pre.sourceCode { overflow-y: visible !important }` beats Bootstrap's `.visually-hidden { overflow: hidden !important }`. As a result, the box computes to `overflow-y: auto`.
- **Fix:** One rule in `styles.css` gives `overflow: hidden !important` back to `pre.sourceCode.visually-hidden`.
- **Why here:** quarto-cli#14816 will skip these blocks on purpose, and Quarto does not change Bootstrap utility classes that authors can use.

I did an axe scan before and after on the three pages. All 20 instances are gone, and nothing is new or worse. The hidden blocks stay 1×1 and clipped in light and dark mode, at 1440×900 and 320×568.

**Check**

- https://deploy-preview-2234.quarto.org/docs/get-started/hello/jupyter.html
- https://deploy-preview-2234.quarto.org/docs/get-started/computations/jupyter.html
- https://deploy-preview-2234.quarto.org/docs/get-started/authoring/jupyter.html

title: Move "Choose your tool" out of the tools-tabset tablist
description:
The `tools-tabset` filter puts a `

Choose your tool

` inside the `ul[role=tablist]`. A tablist can contain only tabs, so axe reports a critical `aria-required-children` error on three pages (`docs/books/`, `docs/websites/`, `docs/websites/website-blog.html`). The `h3` also adds an empty "Choose your tool" entry to the heading outline of each page. This PR: - adds `aria-label="Choose your tool"` to the tablist. - shows the text as `

` outside the list, in a flex row with the tabs. At desktop width, the tabs look the same as before. At 320px, the label is now on its own row, above a 2×2 grid of tabs. An axe scan of the three pages, before and after the change, removes `aria-required-children :: .nav` (3 instances) and shows no new findings.

# Description
Sync of #2229 to `prerelease`.

### Fix heading levels on the listing card pages

title: Fix skipped heading levels in markdown headings
description:
This PR fixes the axe `heading-order` violations that come from `#`-style headings in quarto-web source files: 26 signatures and 36 instances. A full axe scan of this branch shows that all of them are gone.

It covers what is left of the heading-order work after the landing page fix in #2198. Headings that come from templates or scripts, and the raw HTML `<h3>` in the get-started tool chooser, are for a different PR.

### Wrong level

Most fixes change the number of `#`s:

- Pages whose first heading was `###`: `license.qmd`, `docs/faq/rmarkdown.qmd`.
- `### Quick Start` under the title: `extensions/brand.qmd`, `engine.qmd`, `metadata.qmd`.
- The `{.unlisted}` heading on the extension listing pages. `_listing-chooser.qmd` moves this heading into the listing header, so its CSS and JS selectors now look for `h2`.
- Headings one level too deep in `execution-options.qmd`, `shiny/index.qmd`, `shiny/execution.qmd`, `tools/text-editors.qmd`, `tools/jupyter-lab.qmd`, `website-listings.qmd`, `website-navigation.qmd`, and `revealjs/demo/index.qmd`.
- `get-started/index.qmd`: the tutorial step headings changed from `####` to `###`. The size moved to `tutorial.css`, not to a Bootstrap `.hN` class. Pandoc copies a class from the heading onto its section.
- `reference/projects/options.qmd`: added a `## Project` heading above the included `_options.md`, so that its `###` headings have a parent.

### Headings that are really captions

Some headings were labels for one example ("Markdown Syntax", "Output", "Flatly Themed Output"). A change of level does not fix these. When a label is a heading, the text after the example becomes part of the label's section. These labels are now captions:

- `authoring/markdown-basics.qmd`, `authoring/tables.qmd`, `computations/r.qmd`, `output-formats/html-code.qmd`: `filename=` labels on code blocks, or a lead-in sentence before the output.
- `output-formats/html-themes.qmd`: image captions, with `fig-cap-location: top`.

A new "Headings and Example Labels" section in `_style-guide.md` describes these patterns. `.claude/rules/docs-authoring.md` has a short version.

### `julia.qmd` and the `shift-headings` filter

`julia.qmd` used `#` for its top-level sections, which put a second `h1` on the page. The sections are now `##`. The shared partials that `julia.qmd` includes (for example `_jupyter-authoring-tools.md`) start at `##`, and other pages use the same partials at that level. So I added `filters/shift-headings.lua`, adapted from @jjallaire's filter in [quarto-dev/quarto-cli discussion #6695](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/6695#discussioncomment-15611429). It moves the headings in a `::: {.shift-headings by=1}` div down by the given number of levels. It is in `_quarto.yml`, but only `julia.qmd` uses it now. The page also sets `toc-depth: 4` to keep the same sections in the TOC.

### Freeze

I updated `_freeze/` for the changed pages that execute code: `tables`, `execution-options`, `html-code`, and `revealjs/demo`. The two `html-code` figure PNGs changed because the page was rendered again.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Fix dark-mode contrast of inline code in callout titles, tables, and asides
description:
# Description
Sync of #2225 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Fix dark-mode contrast of inline code in callout titles, tables, and asides
In dark mode, inline code outside `p`, `li`, and `td` gets a light chip. This fails [WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#contrast-minimum) (2.4–2.7:1). The chip color is `$code-bg`, which Quarto defaults to `$gray-100`. In `theme-dark.scss`, `$gray-100` is a light grey. This PR sets `$code-bg` to the page background. It also removes the fade on callout headers (opacity 85%), because the fade pulled title code below 4.5:1.

Checked with a full-site before/after axe scan (Quarto 1.11.4, 374 pages): the three dark-mode inline-code contrast findings are gone (23 instances), and nothing is new or worse.

**Check in dark mode**

Code background:

- Callout titles: https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/projects/profiles.html, https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/get-started/authoring/rstudio.html, https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/manuscripts/authoring/rstudio.html (collapsed)
- Margin aside and table headers: https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html
- Table captions: https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/authoring/front-matter.html
- Page navigation: https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/prerelease/1.3/pdf.html (bottom of page)

Other callouts (header fade removed):

- All five types: https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/authoring/callouts.html
- Simple style: https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/tools/text-editors.html
- Collapsed: https://deploy-preview-2225.quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html

title: [Sync to prerelease] Name toolbar buttons in prose and mark their icons decorative
description:
# Description
Sync of #2216 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Name toolbar buttons in prose and mark their icons decorative
Toolbar icons in the get-started RStudio pages had no alt text (8 axe `image-alt` errors). This PR adds a rule for icons in prose: name the control in bold, then show the icon as a decorative image with the `.ui-icon` class. The rule does not use `<kbd>`.

- `theme.scss`, `theme-dark.scss`: add `img.ui-icon`. It extends `.kbd`, so the icon keeps the key-cap look.
- `_style-guide.md`, `.claude/rules/docs-authoring.md`: add the rule.
- 8 icons on 3 pages now use the rule.

A before/after axe scan of the 3 pages shows that all 8 errors are gone, with no new findings.

Other `<kbd>`-wrapped icons (`rstudio-connect`, `shiny/running`, `visual-editor/technical`) already have `alt=""`. This PR does not change them.

## Check on the preview

In light and dark mode, make sure that each icon looks like a key cap and sits on the text line:

- [Tutorial: Hello, Quarto](https://deploy-preview-2216.quarto.org/docs/get-started/hello/rstudio.html): "Render" in step 3 and after it, and "Run Current Chunk"
- [Tutorial: Computations](https://deploy-preview-2216.quarto.org/docs/get-started/computations/rstudio.html): "Render" near the top
- [Tutorial: Authoring](https://deploy-preview-2216.quarto.org/docs/get-started/authoring/rstudio.html): "Render" in the LaTeX and output-formats sections, and "Publish" near the end

title: [Sync to prerelease] Download table: put the full checksum in the DOM, truncate it with CSS
description:
# Description
Sync of #2139 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Download table: put the full checksum in the DOM, truncate it with CSS
The site audit flagged two WCAG failures on `/docs/download/`, both on the checksum cells:

- **aria-allowed-attr** (critical, WCAG 4.1.2): tippy's interactive mode adds `aria-expanded` to the checksum `<div>`, which is invalid on an element with no role.
- **color-contrast** (serious, WCAG 1.4.3): the truncated hash used `--bs-primary` (3.97:1 on white; small text needs 4.5:1).

The deeper problem: the full SHA-256 lived only in a hover tooltip. Keyboard users could not reach it, screen readers never heard it, and copying it meant drag-selecting text inside a floating tooltip.

**The fix:** the cell's text is now the complete hash, and only the rendering truncates (`text-overflow: ellipsis`). The tooltip, tippy init, and JS truncation are gone. The SHA-256 column header links to the release's `checksums.txt`.

We tried a copy button, an `aria-describedby` span, and a `<details>` disclosure before settling here. This version won because it does both things at once with zero interactive machinery:

- **No visual clutter** — the table looks exactly as it does today.
- **The full hash is available to everyone** — screen readers announce all 64 characters, double-click selects the whole hash for copying, find-in-page matches it, and the header link provides the full values at any viewport, since the CSS truncation only affects what's rendered, not what's in the DOM.

Net diff: +17/−17 lines. Axe scan of the page is clean at 1440×900 and 390×844, light and dark.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Fix the landmarks and heading order on the landing page
description:
# Description
Sync of #2198 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Fix the landmarks and heading order on the landing page
## Summary

The landing page (`index.html`) has no main landmark. The page uses `page-layout: custom`, and for that layout Quarto opens a plain `<div>` in place of `<main>` (see quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14839). As a result, all page content is outside a landmark. A screen reader user who moves to the main landmark finds only the navbar and the footer.

This PR wraps the body of `index.qmd` in `<div role="main">`. It fixes 8 axe findings on `index.html`: `landmark-one-main` and 7 `region` findings. Both rules are axe best practices. They relate to WCAG 2.2 [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#info-and-relationships) and [2.4.1 Bypass Blocks](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#bypass-blocks).

The wrapper uses `role="main"`, not a `<main>` element. Quarto finds a `<main>` with `doc.querySelector("main")` and changes it. On this page, a `<main>` element:

- moves the hero "Welcome to Quarto" heading into a generated title block ([`canonicalizeTitlePostprocessor`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7/src/format/html/format-html-title.ts#L198-L241)). The heading loses its hero style.
- adds anchor links to all h2 to h6 headings ([format-html.ts](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7/src/format/html/format-html.ts#L828-L849)).

`role="main"` gives the same landmark, and Quarto does not change it.

The wrapper also changes which elements are direct children of `#quarto-content`. Quarto adds `padding-top: 14px` to those children (0 below 992px). Two rules in `index.css` apply the same padding one level down, so the layout does not change.

### Heading order

The second commit fixes 2 `heading-order` findings (an axe best practice, related to WCAG 2.2 [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#info-and-relationships)). The page went from h1 to h3 two times, and it had two h1s. The new outline is one h1 ("Welcome to Quarto") and seven h2s:

- The two hero taglines are now paragraphs. They introduce the page, but they are not section headings.
- "Hello, Quarto" is now an h2, not a second h1.
- The six feature titles are now h2s. Before, they were h3s, so they looked like subsections of "Hello, Quarto".

`index.css` styles the new h2s with the same values as the old h1 and h3s. The two `.hello-quarto-banner h1` rules in `theme.scss` and `theme-dark.scss` move into `index.css`. No other page uses them.

## Test plan

- [x] Scanned `index.html` with `quarto call axe _site --pages index.html` before and after each commit. The landmark commit removes 8 findings. The heading commit removes 2 findings. There are no new findings, and `index.html` now has 0 findings.
- [x] For each commit, took full-page screenshots before and after, in light and dark mode, at widths of 320, 768, 991, 992, 1200 and 1440 px. All 12 pairs are identical.
- [ ] Opened the page with VoiceOver. The landmarks list shows "main".

The 7 that remain are images with no alt text at all, which a later PR will fix. - No new findings, and all cells completed in both runs.

# Description

## Original PR

## Summary

Two defects in the three hand-written tool chooser strips (get-started, manuscripts, extensions):

- Six logo images had no `alt` attribute. Each image sits next to link text that already names the tool, so `alt=""` marks it as decorative. Fixes axe `image-alt` (WCAG 2.2 1.1.1, Level A).
- The strips carried `role="tablist"`, but the children are page-navigation links, not ARIA tabs. Removed the tab roles, wrapped each list in a `<nav>` with an accessible name, moved a stray `<h3>` out of a `<ul>`, and added `aria-current="page"` to the active link. Fixes axe `aria-required-children` (WCAG 2.2 1.3.1, Level A, critical impact).

Also added `aria-hidden="true"` to the decorative Bootstrap icons in the extensions listing chooser, while touching that markup.

## Test plan

- [x] Rendered affected pages and confirmed the tab strips look the same
- [x] Ran axe against one page per family; both signatures are gone, no new violations
- [x] Clicked through two tutorial pages; the active tab still latches and `localStorage` still holds the choice

title: Document `quarto call axe`, the experimental site accessibility scanner
description:
## Description

Adds `docs/websites/website-accessibility.qmd`, a user-facing page for the
experimental `quarto call axe` command (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14815). 

Also updates `docs/output-formats/html-accessibility.qmd`. Its "Site-wide
accessibility checks" section ended with a paragraph about a mode we
"envision in the future". That paragraph now points at the new page.

## Decisions worth a look

- **The page is deliberately not in the sidebar.** It renders and it enters
  search and `llms.txt`, but an unlisted page under `docs/` gets no left
  sidebar and no breadcrumbs, so it reads full-width. That is the intended
  state while the command is experimental. Wiring it into the Websites
  section is a two-line change to `_quarto.yml`.
- **No guidance on excluding content in source.** The scanner's own generated
  README distinguishes two ledgers: inaccessibility an author chose as part
  of a lesson, versus a problem someone should eventually fix. Only the
  second belongs in the baseline. This page documents the baseline alone and
  says nothing about the first case, because the exclude-in-source pathway
  does not exist yet.
- **The page complements the generated `_axe-checks/README.md` instead of
  repeating it.** The README owns the field-by-field reference for a finding
  and for a baseline entry, and it is regenerated on every scan, so it always
  matches the build that wrote it. The page documents the workflow and links
  to it.
- **The worked example omits one finding.** A scan of the example site also
  reports `region` on `#quarto-skip-link`, on the home page only. That is a
  Quarto bug, not something the example's content causes, and it is filed as
  quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14875. The excerpts leave it out so that regenerating them after the
  fix reproduces the surrounding text unchanged. Everything else in them is
  exactly what the scan wrote, against Quarto 1.11.4.

## Follow-up in quarto-cli

Once this page has a URL, two places in quarto-cli need it (both currently
point at `dev-docs/axe-scan.md`):

1. `news/changelog-1.11.md`, the #14815 entry.
2. `src/command/call/axe/cmd.ts`, the command `.description()`.

The URL is `https://prerelease.quarto.org/docs/websites/website-accessibility.html`
until 1.11 ships.

title: [Sync to prerelease] docs(publish): ambiguous argument '#': move terminal comment to separate line
description:
# Description
Sync of #2180 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### docs(publish): ambiguous argument '#': move terminal comment to separate line
In the quarto publish > gh-pages page the current instructions for creating a gh-pages branch manually has this line:

```
git reset --hard # make sure all changes are committed before running this!
```
However when you run this command as-is you get an error

```
> git reset --hard # make sure all changes are committed before running this!

fatal: ambiguous argument '#': unknown revision or path not in the working tree. Use '--' to separate paths from revisions, like this: 'git <command> [<revision>...] -- [<file>...]'
```

This PR moves the comment on its own separate line before the `git reset` command so the entire chunk can be copy+pasted without an error.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Fix stale quarto-cli release being accepted by release-info
description:
# Description
Sync of #2170 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Fix stale quarto-cli release being accepted by release-info
On 2026-08-17 the GitHub Releases API served inconsistent paginated results to
the `Update Downloads` cron job, and the resolved latest prerelease bounced
across four stale versions over about 100 minutes:

    13:19  1.11.1  (correct)
    13:47  1.2.113
    14:28  0.2.434
    14:43  1.9.10
    14:57  1.5.49
    15:26  1.11.1  (back to correct, stable since)

Each bad value was committed to `main`, synced to `prerelease`, and published,
so the downloads page and the `/download/prerelease/*` redirects advertised
assets from an old release. The 14:43 run also opened #2146, regenerating 63
reference pages against a ten-month-old v1.9.10; it was closed unmerged.

## Root Cause

`getPrerelease()` in `.github/workflows/actions/release-info/index.js` returns
the first release flagged `prerelease` from page 1 of `listReleases`, relying
entirely on the API returning newest-first. The only downstream validation is
that the release has assets, which a ten-month-old release still has. All four
bad values are genuine old quarto-cli releases, so nothing in the payload marks
the response as wrong.

## Fix

A glitched page cannot be told apart from a good one by inspection, so the
check compares against state the API does not control: the version already
committed in the JSON file the run would overwrite. A resolved version older
than the committed one throws, `core.setFailed` fails the step, and
`git-auto-commit-action` never runs, so nothing is committed, synced,
published, or handed to the reference-page workflow. Each check sits before
`processRelease()`, so a rejected run downloads no assets and writes nothing.

Comparison is numeric per segment, since both `1.9.10` and `1.10.2` sort wrong
as strings.

Comparing against the latest stable release was rejected instead: the stable
and prerelease lines cross at every release cycle. Today v1.10.18 is stable
while v1.11.1 is the prerelease, and once the 1.11 line goes stable the latest
stable will exceed the latest prerelease until 1.12.0 ships, so valid data
would be rejected.

The paging loop was also bounded. It was `while(true)` with no page cap and no
empty-page exit, so a repository with no prerelease at all would loop until the
job timed out.

## Test Plan

- [x] `npm test` from `.github/workflows/actions/release-info/` passes both suites
- [x] Each version the API served on 08-17 is rejected against the committed baseline:

      node -e "
      const { assertNotOlder } = require('./.github/workflows/actions/release-info/version-guard');
      const previous = require('./docs/download/_prerelease.json').version;
      for (const bad of ['1.2.113','0.2.434','1.9.10','1.5.49']) {
        try { assertNotOlder('v'+bad, previous, 'x'); console.log('NOT CAUGHT', bad); }
        catch { console.log('caught', bad); }
      }"

- [x] The current correct version is still accepted, so ordinary runs are unaffected
- [x] `zizmor .github/` reports no findings, so `audit-workflows.yml` stays green
- [ ] After merge, the next scheduled `Update Downloads` run completes normally

The original failure cannot be reproduced on demand, since it depends on the
API returning inconsistent pages. The equivalent end-to-end check inverts it:
raise the `version` field in a local copy of `docs/download/_prerelease.json`
above the real latest prerelease, run the action against the live API, and
confirm the step fails with the guard message and writes nothing. Driving that
through a `workflow_dispatch` of `Update Downloads` needs care, because that
workflow commits and pushes once the action succeeds.

Fixes quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14823

# Description
Sync of #2136 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Add link-previews to shortcodes-and-filters listing
Adds [link-previews](https://github.com/ravila4/quarto-link-previews) to the shortcodes-and-filters listing.

The filter gives a Quarto website hover previews for its internal links, the way Quartz digital gardens and Obsidian's page preview do. Hovering a link to another page opens a popover with that page's title block and content, and a link to a section opens the preview scrolled to that heading.

It reuses the tippy.js bundle Quarto already ships for footnote and cross-reference hovers, which is also where the popover theming comes from, so previews track the site theme in light and dark mode. Navigation chrome, external links, footnotes, cross-references and downloads are left alone.

Listing requirements: public GitHub repository, README with installation and usage, MIT license, tagged releases through v0.2.0, and a root `example.qmd`.

Live demo and docs, with the filter running on the site itself: <https://ravila4.github.io/quarto-link-previews/>

The entry is inserted alphabetically between `line-highlight` and `linkate`.

The filter gives a Quarto website hover previews for its internal links, the way Quartz digital gardens and Obsidian's page preview do. Hovering a link to another page opens a popover with that page's title block and content, and a link to a section opens the preview scrolled to that heading.

It reuses the tippy.js bundle Quarto already ships for footnote and cross-reference hovers, which is also where the popover theming comes from, so previews track the site theme in light and dark mode. Navigation chrome, external links, footnotes, cross-references and downloads are left alone.

Listing requirements: public GitHub repository, README with installation and usage, MIT license, tagged releases through v0.2.0, and a root `example.qmd`.

Live demo and docs, with the filter running on the site itself: <https://ravila4.github.io/quarto-link-previews/>

The entry is inserted alphabetically between `line-highlight` and `linkate`.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Add the index extension to the shortcodes and filters listing
description:
# Description
Sync of #2162 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Add the index extension to the shortcodes and filters listing
Adds [quarto-index](https://github.com/jmgirard/quarto-index) to `shortcodes-and-filters.yml`, placed alphabetically between `include-code-files` and `inline-svg`.

The extension gives Quarto documents and books a subject index: authors mark terms with a format-neutral span (`[term]{.index}`, plus `entry=`, `see=`, `see-also=`, `sort=`, `mention=`, `range=` and `index=`), and per-format back-ends realize the index. LaTeX/PDF goes through `imakeidx`; HTML prints the entry tree with letter groups and links each locator back to the marked passage. A Quarto book gets one index for the whole book. In formats with no back-end the marks pass through and emit nothing.

Against the requirements in `docs/extensions/listings/README.md`:

- Hosted from a GitHub repository.
- [README.md](https://github.com/jmgirard/quarto-index/blob/main/README.md) covers installation and usage, with fuller documentation at <https://jmgirard.github.io/quarto-index/>.
- MIT licensed ([LICENSE](https://github.com/jmgirard/quarto-index/blob/main/LICENSE)).

Requires Quarto 1.4 or later. Current release is [v0.1.0](https://github.com/jmgirard/quarto-index/releases/tag/v0.1.0).

title: Add sidebar separators so page navigation stays within sections
description:
The prev/next links at the bottom of each page cross major section boundaries. For example, https://quarto.org/docs/interactive/ links back to "Using Manuscripts", a page in a different guide.

This PR adds `- text: "---"` separators between the top-level subsections of two sidebars in `_quarto.yml`:

- **Guide**: 12 separators, between Authoring, Computations, Tools, Documents, Presentations, Dashboards, Websites, Books, Manuscripts, Interactivity, Publishing, Projects, and Advanced.
- **Reference**: 4 separators, between Formats, Code Cells, Projects, Metadata, and Quarto CLI.

Page navigation drops a prev/next link when the adjacent sidebar item is a separator ([quarto-cli source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7/src/project/types/website/website-navigation.ts#L1211-L1216)). The Extensions sidebar already uses separators this way.

**Visual change to judge**: each separator also renders as a horizontal rule in the sidebar, between the top-level subsections. This matches the look of the Extensions sidebar.

Verified with local renders (Quarto 1.10.18):

- `/docs/interactive/` no longer links back to "Using Manuscripts"; its "Observable JS" next link is unchanged.
- Within-section links are unchanged. For example, `/docs/interactive/ojs/` keeps its "Overview" and "Libraries" links.
- `/docs/reference/cells/cells-ojs` keeps its "Knitr" prev link and no longer links forward into Projects.

Note: AI implemented this change, grounded in local clones of quarto-web and quarto-cli.

title: [Sync to prerelease] docs: set github-actions steps version as variables
description:
# Description
Sync of #2150 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### docs: set github-actions steps version as variables
Setup variables to keep the github actions steps up to date with a single change to one file.

Covered steps: `actions/checkout`, `quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup`, `quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish`, `actions/setup-python`, `r-lib/actions/setup-r`, and `r-lib/actions/setup-renv`. The Python and R versions that the example workflows pin are variables too.

Each value is bumped to the current stable release: `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-python@v7`, Python `3.14`, and R `4.6.1`. The other steps stay at `v2`, which is still their latest major.

Note that there is a "tool" also using an outdated version of the checkout step `_tools/screenshots/examples/quarto-demo/.github/workflows/publish.yml`. That directory is a git subtree of quarto-dev/quarto-demo, so the fix belongs upstream.

Resolves quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14796
