title: refactor: harmonise and fix broken internal links
description:
Related to #1030 and quarto-dev/quarto-cli#8902

This PR does:
- Use path relative to root instead of `../..` in many places -> more straightforward to find the files.
- Use `.qmd` rather than `.html` for internal links -> Quarto replaces `qmd` when needed.
- Remove all hardcoded `https://quarto.org/` "wrongly" used for internal links.
- Fix bad links with `.../`.
- Fix few typos such as three "p" in "appplication" or a missing "k" in "chalboard".

Going forward I would suggest the following for the documentation:
- Use paths relative to root, especially if it means using `../`.
- Use `.qmd` for all internal links. (possible exception: blog posts)

--- 

FYI, for the links check, I used <https://github.com/stevenvachon/broken-link-checker> (a bit outdated regarding the dependencies).

```sh
npm install broken-link-checker -g
# npm uninstall -g broken-link-checker

quarto render --use-freezer
quarto preview --no-watch-inputs --port 3002

file="broken-links-internal.txt"
website="http://127.0.0.1:3002/_site/index.html"
blc --exclude-external --recursive ${website} > ${file}
sed -i '' '/──OK──/d' ${file}
sed -i '' '/^Finished/d' ${file}
sed -i '' '/_ (HTTP_404)/d' ${file} # These are JavaScript links to detect OS/etc. and provide download link to the right asset
awk 'BEGIN {prev=""} {if (prev ~ /^Getting links from/ && $0 !~ /BROKEN/) next; if (NR>1) print prev; prev=$0} END {if (prev !~ /^Getting links from/) print prev}' ${file} > temp && mv -f temp ${file}

```

## Current link status

```txt
Getting links from: http://127.0.0.1:3002/_site/index.html
├─BROKEN─ http://127.0.0.1:3002/_site/docs/authoring/penguins-qmd.embed-preview.html (HTTP_404)
├─BROKEN─ http://127.0.0.1:3002/_site/docs/authoring/penguins-qmd.embed-preview.html#cell-fig-size-scatter (HTTP_404)
├─BROKEN─ http://127.0.0.1:3002/_site/docs/authoring/penguins-qmd.embed-preview.html (HTTP_404)
```

The links are the one created by Quarto when embedding Quarto and Jupyter notebook.
I am probably missing a rendering/computation somewhere locally when using `quarto render --use-freezer` as the links are fine on the outdated preview.
See: https://deploy-preview-1031--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/authoring/notebook-embed.html
- https://deploy-preview-1031--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/authoring/penguins-qmd.embed-preview.html

title: [Sync to prerelease] Dark mode styling
description:
# Description
Sync of #1658 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Dark mode styling
This PR uses Posit's brand for dark mode colors, with AA WCAG color contrast in mind. It also includes some spacing nudges to the homepage, because designers gotta design, I guess.  While that might sound concerning, it's pretty minor stuff... I just utilized bootstrap's grid classes to make things look nice at every breakpoint, which is obviously for both light or dark mode. 

Additional thoughts:
- [ ] I'm not sure how to swap out the navbar logo for a dark mode version.  I tried `![](./logo-dark.png){.dark-content} ![](./logo.png){.light-content}`, but it didn't work. The great news here is the current logo passes for accessibility for dark mode, so we can punt on this now if we need to.  Having said that.... It  _barely_ passes. So I'd love to be able to swap to a much more accessible, dark mode logo as soon as we can. 

- [ ] I'd love to suggest Shiny's light/dark mode switch, seen in the video below.  The Shiny team says this component ready to be ported over whenever we have the time.  


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/633af825-a9fe-44d8-89de-140745bdf4a7

title: Refactor Julia page
description: By now, the docs for the native engine are nicely fleshed out, however there's still somewhat of a discoverability problem, due to the way that the docs page is structured. Visitors will currently see this table of contents: The native engine section, while far longer than the rest, is squeezed into one entry at the bottom, appearing like an afterthought. Also, some parts that thematically belong to both engines look like they belong only to the jupyter engine. In this PR, I've moved the native engine before the Jupyter engine and added a table that clarifies why the native engine should be preferable for most users (this is not to criticize previous efforts, I just think we need to be really clear here as the older engine is still the default, which carries some weight for new users). If someone can think of something that the Jupyter engine has but the native one doesn't, I'll be happy to add that, too. I've also changed heading levels such that the grouping now appears like this, with both engines appearing directly next to each other, and common content moved under Overview: The headings are a bit unusual in that there are multiple H1's on the same page, but due to the spliced in markdown documents that are reused in other sections, it was easier to resolve the hierarchy problems like this, rather than refactoring all pages that splice in the markdown snippets.

title: Minor branding hints
description:
A few minor improvements from a new-ish / casual Quarto user, who got lost in the docs this past week because the HTML Theming page is the first hit for many Google searches

Fixes:

- The HTML Theming page has no direct links to `_brand.yml`; this should probably be the first thing a new / casual user tries, before (`html`-only) "Basic Options?"
- "Basic Options" is written mostly from the perspective of per-document changes, which is a little odd / confusing on a "Theming" page, especially as the rest of the SASS theme variables on the page seem to be describing more site-wide theming
- For someone out of the loop, it's easy to miss that `_brand.yml` is a separate project from Quarto, and all the "Limitations" and references to "the spec" are really confusing. Maybe this is a stretch (feel free to reject / critique this change), but it might have helped me to put the Brand.YML logo at the top of its docs page?

description:
# Description
Sync of #1495 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### add apa_and_amp to shortcodes-and-filters.yml
This is a minimal Quarto filter extension designed to correct narrative APA citations by replacing the ampersand (`&`) with the word `and` in in-text narrative citations. Unlike the broader apaquarto extension, this filter has a focused scope: handling narrative citations for APA-style compliance. It does not include additional formatting features or broader APA-related enhancements. See https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/11545

description:
# Description
Sync of #1219 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Blog - beautiful tables in Typst
I have most of the mechanics for the Typst CSS blog post, a bunch of examples, and a few words.

However, I did some less-than-perfectly-reproducible things in order to get this working:
- Needed _different_ packages installed in order for Great Tables to run, created local `.venv` for it. Something about numpy versions.
- I need to render minimal HTML examples without any website chrome in order to embed them in iframes, because of the mix of languages. Not knowing how to disable the project and do a local build, I instead created a script that touches `_quarto.yml` before render, and removes it after. Surely there is a better way!
- The examples are cluttered with various codes to turn off non-essential output for the snapshot and for the iframe. Some of this could be done from the command line but not all (and I couldn't find a way to turn off the title except `-M title:false`).
- manual iframe sizing
- centering each within a 50% column seems to look okay, still needs nudge with `padding-top` on the Typst snapshot, since that one is generally wider/shorter

Ignoring these warts, it's pretty easy to add new examples and at least awkwardly reproducible.

title: [Sync to prerelease] Suggest linux users put execs in ~/.local/bin
description:
# Description
Sync of #1118 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Suggest linux users put execs in ~/.local/bin
On many Linux distributions, both `~/bin` and `~/.local/bin` will be automatically put on PATH, thanks to this common snippet in the /etc/profile file:

    PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
    if test "$HOME" != "/" ; then
    for dir in $HOME/bin/$CPU $HOME/bin $HOME/.local/bin/$CPU $HOME/.local/bin ; do
        test -d $dir && PATH=$dir:$PATH
    done
    fi

So, it is prudent to suggest that users check this before modifying their .profile file. Furthermore, while `~/bin` has been informally used for a while, `~/.local/bin` is part of the XDG Base Directory Spec, which is increasingly embraced by the Linux ecosystem.

title: Feature/confluence docs feedback jj
Confluence Docs
description:
This looks great! So excited to get this into people's hands :-) This PR makes some suggested revisions --- nearly all of the original content is still there (save for stuff about project workflow that isn't as applicable to Confluence) but I've added some introductory material and some info on using the "preview formats" for both documents and projects.

I would also suggest that for the time being we move this to be a peer of the other v1.3 preview feature documentation here: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/tree/main/docs/prerelease/1.3 (we are no longer using the `{{< include >}}` from the publish directory which will make this easier).

Once we've iterated on this and are happy with the basic flow, I think we should add a screenshot and perhaps diagram at the beginning to sell the feature a bit more (perhaps a `qmd` on the left and a published confluence page that includes code, tables, etc. on the right?). Besides getting people excited about the feature, I think this will also help clarify in a more tactile way exactly what it is doing.

We should also work with @dragonstyle on getting a `quarto create website confluence` command added (and then perhaps split out "creating a new site" and "publishing an existing site" within the docs where the former uses this command.

In terms of diagrams, we might be able to get these working by just adding `mermaid-format: png` to the format when we render for confluence? I could definitely be wrong about this though (more on mermaid options here: https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/diagrams.html#mermaid-formats)

title: Fix Hugging Face wrong link
Add R and Python dependencies management for easier local rendering of docs with computation
description:
This PR adds some tooling to manage the R and python environment more easily. @cwickham I suggest we test this together, and I can demo how it works. This should allow us to work from Windows Mac or Linux the same, and allow also contributor to be able to locally render a change. We could even think of some automation from CI now that setting up some computation environment is easier. 

First, documentation has been added in the README.md. Happy to move that somewhere else if desired. 

Then, we currently use two tools to manage R and Python dependencies. 

## For R

We use **renv** for the `quarto-web` project and it is used only for R dependencies. 

To speed up the loading time, the project uses explicit type for dependencies - this means all the dependencies the project needs are defined in `DESCRIPTION` file. Adding one dependency requires to add to this file. 

R has been updated to 4.3.2 and all R dependencies have been updated to latest. This means that when some files with knitr engine will be re-rendered in the future, the `_freeze` folder will be updated as some rendering may store version dependant information (like HTML widgets dependencies). But that is the all point of `freeze: true` I guess. 

As usual with **renv**, a `.Rprofile` is defined to activate automatically the project library. If **renv** is not yet installed, it will be installed and then project library set up. 

**I believe to test this PR correctly, the best thing is to remove the project library (`renv` folder) and then let the new configuration applies**

## For python, 

As with `quarto-cli` test environment, this project now uses **pipenv** (https://pipenv.pypa.io/en/latest) to handle the python depdencies and manage the virtualenvironment. 

A `.env` file defines a configuration so that virtual environment is store locally to the project. This is not the default for `pipenv` but it seems probably more aligned with current workflow. 

`PipFile` will be the equivalent of `DESCRIPTION` to track the dependencies we need. `pipenv sync` creates a `Pipfile.lock` with pinned dependency tree (like `renv.lock`). 

Unlike **renv** though, the python virtual env won't be loaded by default when running. `pipenv shell` will activate it for the current shell, otherwise `pipenv run quarto render ...` is a way to run Quarto command with the virtual environment. 
Though it can also be activate usually from the `.venv/` scripts if one prefer. 

Note that **reticulate** knows about `pipenv` and so it will use the same virtual environment for Python chunk in knitr engine documents. 

**`requirement.txt` has been removed from git, and ignored because it is no more used as `Pipfile` is the one to track our addition, and `Pipfile.lock` the one used to restore same versions of all deps.**

## About current documentation

I did not rebuild the whole website using those new deps. I checked that all the `import` and `library` found were covered in `Pipfile` and `DESCRIPTION`. If I missed some, it will be easy to add them now. 

This means that when we'll need to re-render some part of the website, some dependencies may have an impact on the `_freeze` content, and we'll need to update it. That is all. 

You could though at some point rebuild from scratch the whole website (removing `_freeze` and then `quarto render`), but then we will need to check all pages of the website to correct output. I believe we did `freeze: true` to always have a working website.  I could also set up a weekly CI running the whole website to see if we have some rendering error or not. 
Anyhow, to be discussed.  

Hope this is clear. Let's discuss this live when we can - happy to answer any question, and also clarify the doc.

title: Updates from changelog: Website
description:
[Guide > Websites > Website Navigation](https://deploy-preview-968--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/websites/website-navigation.html): 

- [x] In website projects, a single sidebar with a `id` property will no longer be used as a global sidebar. It will instead be used as a sidebar for only pages which specify that `id` or pages linked to from the sidebar.
- [x] Add support for `navbar > toggle-position` to control whether the responsive navbar toggle appears on the right or the left.
- [x] Add support for setting `page-navigation: true|false` in either a page or in `_metadata.yml`. This allows individual pages or sections of a website to control whether `page-navigaation` appears.
- [x] Add support for `bread-crumbs: true|false` to control whether bread crumbs are displayed. Add support for display of breadcrumbs on full width (non-mobile) pages when `bread-crumbs` is true. Default value is true.
- [x] ([#5283](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/5283)): Add support for setting `repo-actions: false` in a document to prevent the display of repository actions on a specific page.
- [x] ([#5964](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/5964)): Add support for `repo-link-target` and `repo-link-rel` to control the corresponding attributes of repo-action links.

[Guide > Websites > Website Search](https://deploy-preview-968--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/websites/website-search.html):

- [x] Add support for `show-item-context` key within the `search` key to control whether page parents are display next to items in search results. Pass `tree`, `parent`, `root`, or boolean (if you pass true, `tree` is the default).
- [x] ([#5763](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/5763)): Add support for a keyboard shortcut to launch search (defaults to `s`, `f` or `/`). Use `search` > `keyboard-shortcut` to override with your own key(s).
- [x] ([#7796](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/7796)): Allow providing placeholder text using the language key `search-text-placeholder`

[Guide > Websites > Website Tools](https://deploy-preview-968--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/websites/website-tools.html):

- [x] ([#5389](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/5389)): Allow a website project to provide a default image used in social metadata tags.
- [x] ([#5251](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/5251)): Allow individual pages to specify `image: false` to prevent image discover for Twitter and Open Graph metadata.
- [x] ([#5624](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/5624)): Add support for localized Cookie Consent (using either the document's language or by specifying the language explicitly under the cookie consent key).

title: WIP Updates to Crossref Highlights
description:
Expands on existing crossref highlights on the [pre-release highlights page](https://deploy-preview-919--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/prerelease/1.4/), but also designed to help with the merge into main docs when 1.4 is released. Specifically:
* Adds a [Cross-Reference Div Syntax](https://deploy-preview-919--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/authoring/cross-references-divs.html) page. The content type sections on this page (e.g. Figures, Tables etc) can move into the relevant pages/sections Authoring > Figures#cross-references, Authoring > Scholarly Writing > Cross References when 1.4 is released. The remaining content then becomes more of a "things you can do with div syntax you can't do other ways".
* Adds a [Custom Cross Reference Types](https://deploy-preview-919--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/authoring/cross-references-custom.html) page. When 1.4 is released, we might consider this becoming part of a "Customizing Cross References" page, which pulls in some of the existing customizing bits (like Chapter Numbers and Options) from the existing Cross References page.
* Adds a [Cross-References for Executable Code Blocks](https://deploy-preview-919--mystifying-jepsen-fa4396.netlify.app/docs/authoring/cross-references-listings.html) page, that will become a section of Authoring > Scholarly Writing > Cross References > Code Listings when 1.4 is released.

Nothing is exposed beyond the links from the pre-release highlights so it can be merged now.

title: dashboards: Add MyNorfolk static R example
description:
If you'd like another R-based, static, but regularly updated, dashboard to showcase, I used the [MyNorfolk requests data](https://data.norfolk.gov/Government/MyNorfolk/nbyu-xjez) to build a dashboard for monitoring the status of citizen requests in Norfolk, VA.

Because the source data is updated daily, the dashboard is built using GitHub Actions (with the help of [renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) and [targets](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/)) and published to <https://grrrck.quarto.pub/mynorfolk-dash> when the source data updates.

The complete source is on GitHub at [gadenbuie/mynorfolk-dash](https://github.com/gadenbuie/mynorfolk-dash) and I plan to built both a Quarto-Shiny and a pure Shiny for R version of the dashboard to showcase the connection between Quarto's dashboard components and their counterparts in the Shiny ecosystem.

title: Add  quarto-ieee template for IEEE transaction/journal
description:
IEEE is one of the most famous scientific associations in the fields of engineering. It is the publisher of hundreds of peer-reviewed transactions, journals and magazines in various fields (e.g. electronics, computer engineering, control, biomedical, etc.).
This adds the [quarto-ieee] template, which supports the [`IEEEtran`](https://ctan.org/pkg/ieeetran)  LaTeX document class for PDF output. In addition, the HTML output is supported, and attempts to mimic as closely as possible the paper layout seen on [IEEEXplore<sup>®</sup>](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/).

The [quarto-ieee] template is hosted on Github, includes a [`README.md`](https://github.com/dfolio/quarto-ieee#readme), and is licensed under the MIT.

[quarto-ieee]: <https://github.com/dfolio/quarto-ieee>

title: docs: explicit reference to filetype for .mmd File Includes
description:
Makes more explicit that an .mmd file can be used as an external source when including a Mermaid diagram in a .qmd document, as this is made more explicit for .dot files in the current version of the docs.

Mermaid and Graphviz diagrams can be included in `.qmd` documents from external files.

In the docs an example is given for how to achieve this
using a Graphviz diagram defined in a `.dot` file.

This minor change makes it more explicit that an appropriate filetype
that would achieve the same for a Mermaid diagram is `.mmd`.

The `.mmd` filetype is mentioned two sections previous
in the context of specific editors (RStudio, VS Code).
Readers of the docs are likely to benefit from seeing
the relevant filetypes close to their implementation in the File Include section of the docs,
especially if they are not users of RStudio or VS Code and
may miss those previous sections.

description:
Address #20. I think I got them all! I tried to follow the guidelines I found in the sources provided by @spcanelon. That means I generally erred on the side of being too descriptive, but I also (generally) tried to stick to talking about what the point of the image was. Also, if a version of the same figure showed up multiple times in a page, I shortened the general description in later alt texts and focused on the details/differences.

@jjallaire, @dragonstyle:
* Can we get a live preview of these changes through Netlify? Or should I just host it on a fork?
* I only committed the changes to the `qmd` themselves. How is the site built? Should I render it locally and commit those changes, as well?

Additionally:
* Fixes #22 - the paths were just missing the 'docs' prefix. 
* A few typos I ran into
* There were a couple of images missing at the bottom of [books/book-authoring](https://quarto.org/docs/books/book-authoring.html). I copied the images over from [output-formats/ms-word.html#templates](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/ms-word.html#templates) into `books/images` and fixed those links.
* The first line in the example in  [visual_editor/technical.qmd#equations](https://quarto.org/docs/visual-editor/technical.html#equations) is wrong - it should be "The solution to \sqrt{x} = 26 is x = 676". I pushed a fixed version of the image: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6981612/128639881-9eeea9c6-00ba-4b09-ab82-0976550d6764.png)
Github is adding a ton of whitespace above the image for some reason, but it doesn't show up in the preview. I used the Dreamweaver theme to take the screenshot. That's the one you used, right @jjallaire?

Add Neovim next to RStudio and VS Code
description:
I had some time in the festive season to work extensively on [quarto-nvim](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-nvim) and added a bunch of really cool features. This means the quarto extension for neovim is now (almost) on par with the vs code extension. In some places in can even do more.

This also means that quarto in neovim is now more than just syntax highlighting, so the quarto website could be updated to reflect this. I would like to give neovim it's own section next to the ones about RStudio and VS Code to showcase the full functionality that goes beyond being just a text editor.

As of now, quarto-nvim can do

- code completion (optionallly also for any language, not just R, python, julia. For example lua or haskell)
- documetation hovers
- go to definition
- quarto preview
- search the quarto website for documentation
- export all code chunks as standalone scripts

Here are some [screenshots](https://github.com/jmbuhr/quarto-nvim-kickstarter#screenshots).

This is not the final pull request, just an initial proposal to ask if you would be open to it.

If you don't already have your own neovim configuration, the easiest way to play aroud with `quarto-nvim` is to use this kickstarter configuration: https://github.com/jmbuhr/quarto-nvim-kickstarter (for code execution in combination with https://github.com/jmbuhr/tmux-kickstarter)

description:
Hi Quarto team,

I was recently using Quarto to document a Python package I am developing. It took me some time to figure out how to get Quarto to use my virtual environment. Eventually, I realized I needed to install a kernel within my virtual environment. Documenting how to do this could be helpful as other users may run into the same problem.

I have added a new section to the docs/computations/python.qmd page to explain how to use Quarto with a virtual environment.

Note that it is already documented how to select your kernel:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/81540c76b5c84be6e3e5f402c7796e55de58f6a5/docs/computations/python.qmd#L83-L105

I hope that my PR makes it clear to users that you need to install a kernel in your virtual environment.

title: Make it clear to the reader how to change page properties in Word
description:
To PDF produced by LaTeX, I can change the page by having

```
format:
  pdf:
    papersize: a4paper
```

in the YAML header. I was looking how to do the same with Word and it strikes me that the documentation doesn't clear states it. [Pandoc's manual](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html) says

> The contents of the reference docx are ignored, but its stylesheets and document properties (including margins, page size, header, and footer) are used in the new docx.

This PR add a paragraphs about changing document properties.

**Help needed!**

- [ ] Create correct screenshot. I don't MS Word in my machine.
- [ ] Replace wrong screenshot.

title: Correct possibly misleading info on bibliography file extensions
description:

> A bibliographic data source, for example a *BibTeX (.bib)* file

However, this description may be possibly misleading b/c Pandoc uses `*.bib` file extension for BibLaTeX and `*.bibtex` for BibTeX: https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#specifying-bibliographic-data

chore: refresh frozen revealjs site_libs for Quarto 1.12.1
description:
The live sites serve an old reveal.js line-highlight plugin even though they are rendered with Quarto 1.12.1. quarto.org and prerelease.quarto.org both deliver a `line-highlight.js` that is byte-identical to the copy tracked in `_freeze/site_libs/revealjs`, not to the one shipped in 1.12.1. It showed up in the deploy preview of #2340, where the `code-line-fragment-indices` example ran the highlight steps in the wrong order.

With `freeze: true`, rendering a page that has frozen results copies `_freeze/site_libs` over the freshly generated `site_libs`. The revealjs runtime tracked there wins over the one from the Quarto version doing the render, see quarto-dev/quarto-cli#10391. The tracked copy predated 1.12.1: reveal.js core, the notes, quarto-support and reveal-menu plugins, and the line-highlight plugin all differed from a fresh 1.12.1 render. Both publish jobs render with the latest prerelease, and `main` and `prerelease` carry the same freezer tree, so one refresh covers both.

`_freeze/site_libs/revealjs` was deleted and the five frozen revealjs pages were re-rendered with 1.12.1, so the freezer regenerates it. The frozen results of those pages are unchanged: re-executing them only altered random widget ids and figure bytes.

# Description
Sync of #2346 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### chore: refresh frozen revealjs site_libs for Quarto 1.12.1
The live sites serve an old reveal.js line-highlight plugin even though they are rendered with Quarto 1.12.1. quarto.org and prerelease.quarto.org both deliver a `line-highlight.js` that is byte-identical to the copy tracked in `_freeze/site_libs/revealjs`, not to the one shipped in 1.12.1. It showed up in the deploy preview of #2340, where the `code-line-fragment-indices` example ran the highlight steps in the wrong order.

With `freeze: true`, rendering a page that has frozen results copies `_freeze/site_libs` over the freshly generated `site_libs`. The revealjs runtime tracked there wins over the one from the Quarto version doing the render, see quarto-dev/quarto-cli#10391. The tracked copy predated 1.12.1: reveal.js core, the notes, quarto-support and reveal-menu plugins, and the line-highlight plugin all differed from a fresh 1.12.1 render. Both publish jobs render with the latest prerelease, and `main` and `prerelease` carry the same freezer tree, so one refresh covers both.

`_freeze/site_libs/revealjs` was deleted and the five frozen revealjs pages were re-rendered with 1.12.1, so the freezer regenerates it. The frozen results of those pages are unchanged: re-executing them only altered random widget ids and figure bytes.

title: docs: explain that a format-links object renames that format's link
description:
From Quarto 1.12, a `format-links` entry written as an object (`format`, `text`, `icon`) renames the link for that format, and other rendered formats keep their default links. Before, the default link was added as well, so a renamed `typst` link showed up twice, as "PDF" and "Typst", unless the list also had a plain-string entry. The example in "Specifying Formats to Link" listed `- html`, which avoided the duplicate.

Remove `- html` from that example and explain how the two kinds of entry combine: an object renames a link, and plain strings limit the links to the formats they name.

Targets `prerelease` because the fix ships in 1.12.

Companion to quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15312

description:
# Description
Sync of #2341 to `prerelease`.

## Original PR

### Add webmcp extension to the listing
Adds [webmcp](https://github.com/alexanderwiebe/quarto-webmcp) to `shortcodes-and-filters.yml`, between `watermark` and `webr`.

It is a filter extension for HTML output that exposes a site's content to in-browser AI agents through [WebMCP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp). Every page registers tools for the site's pages, posts and search. A post with an `agent:` block in its front matter also gets tools for its summary, audience, claims and evidence, and sources. A post-render script writes a search index and an `llms.txt`.

Listing requirements: hosted on GitHub, README with install steps and usage examples, MIT license (`LICENSE`), and an `example.qmd`. Latest release: v0.2.0. CI renders the example site and `example.qmd` with the current Quarto release and pre-release. In use on https://systemsbyaj.com.

title: docs: Pandoc 3.13 changes for Quarto 1.12
description:
Quarto 1.12 updates Pandoc from 3.10 to 3.13. Some of its changes alter existing documents, and its Typst writer reads two new attributes, so the docs need to follow.

- The 1.12 pre-release highlights mention the Pandoc update in one line, like earlier releases, and list under "When upgrading" only the changes users must act on: duplicate bibliography keys, Word bookmark names, MathML in HTML without Bootstrap, and the Typst 0.15 requirement for `QUARTO_TYPST`. Other changes stay in the changelog (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15351).
- The HTML page now says that math renders as MathML in HTML without the Bootstrap theme (`minimal: true`, `theme: none`, `theme: pandoc`). It was plain text with Pandoc 3.10.
- The Typst page documents `typst-label` on divs and `lang` on spans. `typst-label` is shown as a way to target a div from raw Typst, for example with a show rule. Cross-references keep using Quarto identifiers, as Quarto's crossref labels don't use it.
- The PowerPoint page no longer lists tables for the Content with Caption layout, as a slide with text followed by a table now uses Title and Content. Two-column slides with a table still use Comparison.
- A new `.claude/rules/release-highlights.md` rule keeps highlights short and asks to check the quarto-cli PR before describing a dependency's behavior change. It is also proposed directly on `main`.

Targets `prerelease` because these changes ship in 1.12, and should merge after quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15320.

## Test Plan

- [x] Each new example rendered with a Quarto dev build using Pandoc 3.13 and with Quarto 1.11.9 (Pandoc 3.10): the Typst label and `#text(lang:)` appear only with 3.13, the three non-Bootstrap HTML setups get MathML only with 3.13, text followed by a table gets Title and Content only with 3.13, and a two-column slide with a table gets Comparison with both
- [x] The edited pages and the pages that include the 1.12 highlights render with `--profile prerelease-docs`, and the new links resolve to existing anchors

Companion to quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15320
